verdict.rationale: Jitsu documents an official hosted MCP server at https://use.jitsu.com/mcp that lets AI agents create destinations, wire up streams, inspect Live Events and edit Functions. Interactive clients authenticate via OAuth 2.1 and receive scoped, revocable tokens, while headless and CI environments use a personal API key. A probe confirms the MCP docs page exists. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that agents successfully connect and operate via the MCP server.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can connect an agent via an official MCP server

citations.quote: Jitsu runs an MCP server, so AI agents can manage your pipeline directly: create destinations, wire up streams, inspect Live Events, and edit Functions.
Point your agent at `https://use.jitsu.com/mcp`, approve it once in the browser, and it can run your data pipeline for you.
For interactive clients, authentication is OAuth 2.1 — you don't paste an API key.
In CI and other headless environments the browser flow can't run. There you authenticate with a personal API key instead
Approve it once and the client gets a scoped, revocable token.
